title: LL5-RAMP: capped table growth improves time at the same low-source memory point

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), the single LL5-RAMP algorithm/configuration of proof.md (finite branch n<2^32; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), z=ceil(log2 r), m=floor(21533r/100000)-10z, dl=ceil(115567r/100000)+200z, Hcap=floor(543r/100000), kappa=ceil(log2(m+4))+3, profile v_i=dl+min(floor(3i/4),Hcap), full five-input widths5v_i-v_(i+1)-kappa and four binary remainder levels, with all hard budgets and all-modulus decoders) recovers the full secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY branch including retries, failures, discarded copies and aborts, total charged sequential work is T(N,s)=O(2^((3967/1000)sqrt n)). The exact uniform envelope B_T(n)=2^((3967/1000)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 and an absolute outside constant. Section14 charges the varying-length enumerators by per-level nonreused source sets and uses5^4>2^9 plus exact rational gaps to absorb polynomial factors. All source/extraction, classical processing, circuit generation, lookup, decoding, initialization, reset, measurement and addressing costs are included. This holds jointly with the other resource and zero-tolerance claims for this same configuration.

For the same LL5-RAMP algorithm/configuration of proof.md, every N>=2 and s, n=ceil(log2 N), peak classical allocation on EVERY branch is S_C(N,s)=O(2^((2903/2500)sqrt n)) bits, including retained full-label tables, bounded five-list prefixes, heaps, buffers, extraction scratch and streamed decoder records. The exact uniform envelope B_C(n)=2^((2903/2500)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 and an absolute outside constant. This holds jointly with full-secret success at least1-2^-8 and all other resource and zero-tolerance claims.

For the same LL5-RAMP algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant, including the depth-first index registers and all ancillas. The envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL5-RAMP algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded copy and every failed or aborted attempt, is O(2^((1/2) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The main-branch hard cap is Q <= n Ccap + K = O(n^3 5^m), with Ccap,K,m defined in proof.md; the proved upper coefficient q*232193/100000 is strictly below1/2 and absorbs its polynomial factor. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((1/2) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same LL5-RAMP algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
